prompt: One wide, diagram-like landscape illustration reading left to right. At the far left, a cutaway factory hall where an assembly line builds identical compact shop boxes a few metres square — each already fitted out with built-in shelving, ceiling lights and an air-conditioning unit — with one finished capsule being loaded onto a flatbed truck and several more stacked and waiting. In the centre, a crane lowers one finished capsule onto a city plaza while a thick cable plugs it into a socket in the ground; in the background the same box appears on a waterfront promenade and in a car park, and a faded outline with an upward arrow shows a capsule being hoisted away again, conveying the pop-up idea of a shop that exists somewhere for a while and then doesn't. At the far right, a cutaway of the placed capsule shows customers helping themselves from shelves with no till, no queue and no staff room — just a single robotic arm running the shop, beside a small control desk with one operator and a bank of screens. Dotted signal lines fan out from that console to every capsule in the scene, and the factory line terminates not in a crowd of new employees but in more identical boxes rolling out, so the whole picture reads as one story: a shop manufactured as a product, placed anywhere and removed as easily, and grown by building more boxes that a single machine runs all at once.
